Notes: Pinkas HaKehillot: probable Jewish settlement in the seventeenth century; documents mention Jews leasing distilleries; year 1650 is the century midpoint and presence is described as probable
Town had 2134 inhabitants: 1063 Catholics; 1066 Jews; 5 Protestants
About 5000 Jews at outbreak of WWII (approximate); other sources say about half of 9000-12500 inhabitants; Pinkas: Jewish organized community with Gur and Alexander hasidic synagogues

German occupation September 1939: more than 1000 Jews killed in first days (Pinkas estimate; Jewish virtual library says 65 shot; local site says about 1000 and 77 burned alive); death toll not population
After September 13 1939 not one Jew remained in the city (women and children permitted to leave; men killed)

Postwar: from a community of more than 5000 only a few hundred survivors remained (mostly survivors from the Soviet Union); no community reconstituted; not a documented resident count for Wyszków; year approximate (postwar)
Jewish cemetery established beginning of 19th century; last known Jewish burial 1939; Holocaust memorial made of gravestones dedicated 1997
